claim: `person/email/action/email-action.domain.ts` models archiving, forwarding and skipping as three of its five actions. The 54 code rules do not. Filing is a key of its own holding `archive` or `skip`, forwarding names who receives the mail, and `actions` admits only `notify` and `unsubscribe`. They were landed on the format's shape rather than the domain's, because that is what the data is.

evidence:
The two akasha pages already disagree in writing. `email-rule-code.page-type.ts` carries `Filing is a key of its own rather than an action.` and the absence `There is no forward action.`, while `email-action.domain.ts` carries `domain/email-action-archive`, `domain/email-action-forward` and `domain/email-action-skip` among its five parts. So this is a tension between two pages inside akasha rather than between akasha and anything outside it.

The markdown rule set this was first read off is gone. `pages/rules-engine-rule-set/email-rule.rules-engine-rule-set.md` said the same split, and declared the three keys separately: `email-rule-code-filing` required over `archive` and `skip`, `email-rule-code-actions` as `list(select(lower-kebab-case), max 2)` over `notify` and `unsubscribe`, and `email-rule-code-forward-to-slug` as a relation onto `person`. Nothing reads that file now, the `rules-engine-rule-set` page type has been taken away, and `email-rule-code.page-type.ts` carries the split by itself.

The data agrees with the format. Over all 54 `.email-rule-code.ts` pages: `filing` is on 54, 52 archiving and 2 skipping; `actions` is on 5 and is `["unsubscribe"]` every time; `forwardTo` is on 6 and is `jenny` every time; `delay` is on 1 and is `15m`. Nothing writes archiving, skipping or forwarding as an action, so modelling them as actions would have invented values no rule states.

Not measured: whether anything reads the email actions as one vocabulary, in which case the five action domains and the three keys need reconciling rather than recording.
